chapter: Germany, Buck's death and ideas about life
title: MC at the Kaiserslautern club: You're prejudiced
summary: Hosting a revue for a mixed audience, he faces a deliberate silence and tells them they are prejudiced, then leaves.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Getting to Kaiserslautern, I can't believe what I run into when I get to Kaiserslautern, 'cause a woman there she knew me. She's the woman who brought the / fellow here to write my life story. She's out of the services now at this time and she knew me. Then here comes another guy that works in the

"South Pacific" the play, a dancer, he knew me and he was there in Kaiserslauternand he had to boost me up to her concerning what they had charged me against that I was not the fault of. The club was prejudiced, seemingly, because they wouldn't keep quiet when I come out to M.C. the show and I was M.C.-ing the show he was with that I had and the show was built around me, you know.

So I'm M.C.-ing the show and when I got on the floor to speak, everybody was noisy, and it's a mixed club now, mixed club, Officer's Club, too. They got white and black in there, you know. I'm standing out on the floor to use the mike to introduce the show, who we got on the show and all, I got Mr. and Mrs. Valente, Katerina Valente's mother and father and her husband is on this show that I'm on in Kaiserslautern, and would you believe that when I went on the floor, intending to introduce the show, I got it all assembled and everything and everybody keeps quiet, but I stand there, and

they must have been thinking, "What's he standing there for?" They all kept quiet to see what I was going to say. Just like say, "Let's see what he's going to say." Look like they all got together and did that. Quiet. And I just said two words "You're prejudiced. Don't jibe me with nothin', you're prejudiced." That was my thought and I walked off. What did I say that for?

When I got upstairs, there's a balcony here -- when I come up to my dressing room, one guy tried to stop me. I go in the dressing room, get my bag and my briefcase and I'm going to cut out and go back and get on the bus and come back to Kaiserslautern, you know. Back to the city. I'm out in the outskirts. I'm out in -- what's the name of this airport -- it ain't -- it's kind of a bad reputation anyway.
But when I go get in the bus, while the rest of the show goes on, you going to do it, but I'll be in the thing waiting for you.
